subject: general
question: Which of the following is the primary reason why copper is widely used as a conductor in electrical wiring?

options.text: Copper has high resistance to electricity.
Copper has a low melting point.
Copper has low resistance and high conductivity.
Copper is available in abundance and is also cheap.

solution:
The correct answer is __Copper has low resistance and high conductivity.__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Copper__ is widely used in electrical wiring due to its excellent electrical properties.
 
• Copper has low electrical resistance, allowing electricity to flow easily.
 
• Its high conductivity makes it efficient for transmitting electrical energy.
 
• Copper is ductile, meaning it can be easily shaped into wires.
 
• It is resistant to corrosion, ensuring a longer lifespan for electrical applications.
 
• Copper’s thermal conductivity also helps in dissipating heat generated during electrical transmission.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

 
• **Aluminum vs Copper:**

 
 
• Aluminum is also used for electrical wiring, but it has higher resistance and lower conductivity compared to copper.
 
• Copper is preferred for most applications due to its superior performance.
 
 
 
• **Gold as a conductor:**
 
 
• Gold has excellent conductivity but is rarely used due to its high cost.
 
• Gold is mainly used in specialized applications such as high-precision electronic components.
 
 
 
• **Silver as a conductor:**
 
 
• Silver has the highest conductivity of all metals but is expensive, limiting its use to specialized applications.
 
• Copper strikes the best balance between cost and performance for everyday electrical wiring.
